title: On Demand magnetic-Doppler nuclear frequency comb memory for hard X-ray photons
authors: Yanli Shi, Xiwen Zhang, Yuri Shvyd'ko, Olga Kocharovskaya
abstract: Nuclear quantum memories in the hard X-ray regime offer some key advantages over their optical counterparts, such as broader bandwidth and lower background noise. A Doppler frequency comb protocol has been theoretically proposed [X. Zhang \textit{et al.}, Phys. Rev. Lett. \textbf{123}, 250504 (2019)] and recently demonstrated experimentally [S. Velten \textit{et al.}, Sci. Adv. \textbf{10}, eadn9825 (2024)] for the storage and retrieval of X-ray photons. However, achieving on-demand retrieval remains challenging because of the requirement for precise and synchronous mechanical motion of multiple absorbers. We propose a hybrid, magnetic-Doppler nuclear frequency comb composed of Doppler-shifted resonant absorbers with lifted nuclear spin degeneracy, which expands the Doppler comb structure. By synchronously reversing the directions of both the magnetic fields and absorber velocities, the system achieves time-reversed phase evolution dynamics that allows for efficient on-demand photon retrieval with significantly reduced mechanical complexity.
summary: The paper proposes a magnetic-Doppler nuclear frequency comb memory for storing hard X-ray photons. It overcomes the difficulty of on-demand retrieval by introducing a mechanism that requires synchronously reversing both the internal magnetic field and absorber velocities. This hybrid approach significantly reduces mechanical complexity while maintaining high storage efficiency.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is achieving efficient, on-demand retrieval of hard X-ray photons stored in quantum memories.
main_result: A hybrid magnetic-Doppler nuclear frequency comb protocol allows for on-demand storage and retrieval by synchronously reversing both the internal magnetic field and absorber velocities.
method: The method involves engineering a time-reversed phase evolution dynamic by controlling two external parameters (magnetic field and velocity) simultaneously, rather than relying solely on mechanical motion.
model_or_system: The system utilizes nuclear transitions in ${}^{57}	ext{FeBO}_3$ absorbers, forming a hybrid comb structure incorporating both Doppler shifts ($\Delta\omega_D$) from motion and hyperfine splittings ($\Delta\omega_Z$) from the strong internal magnetic field.
key_observables: Storage efficiency ($\eta$), fidelity ($F$), bandwidth (e.g., $3\Delta\omega$ or $6\Delta\omega$), and the retrieval amplitude $	ext{B}_{	ext{out}}(t)$.
important_parameters: The required simultaneous reversal of both hyperfine magnetic fields ($B_{	ext{hf}}$) and absorber velocities ($\mathbf{v}_n$). The efficiency can reach up to 54% under optimal conditions.
main_assumptions: On-demand retrieval necessitates the simultaneous reversal of both $B_{	ext{hf}}$ and $\mathbf{v}_n$; partial reversal is insufficient. Quadrupole interaction in ${}^{57}	ext{FeBO}_3$ can be neglected at low temperatures.
figures_summary: Figures compare quantum memory efficiencies ($\eta$) and fidelities ($F$) for static vs. on-demand configurations (C-NFC, S-NFC, D-NFC), illustrating the performance gains from active switching.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the limitations of traditional Doppler frequency combs for on-demand retrieval. It then proposes and details the hybrid magnetic-Doppler NFC using ${}^{57}	ext{FeBO}_3$. The core mechanism involves deriving the time-reversed dynamics enabled by simultaneous field/velocity reversal, leading to performance comparisons between different comb configurations (C-NFC vs D-NFC).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum light storage and retrieval using solid-state systems, which is a major area of research at the intersection of AMO physics and quantum optics. The use of hyperfine structure to simplify mechanical requirements is particularly novel.
